purpose: Per-role symbolic-tooling bindings. Capability, not ceremony: each entry adds something a role could not otherwise do, and none of it adds a step to the loop.
tool_timeout_note: Serena defaults to 240s (minimum 10s), which is far too long inside a loop. Hangs are bounded structurally — apply_ex hands every call to a single-threaded TaskExecutor and waits on future.result(timeout) — so this is about how long a wedge is allowed to cost, not whether it terminates. The per-request LSP timeout derives as this minus 5.
reliable_languages_note: Serena's own suite permanently disables BSL and F# and disables Kotlin on CI, which is the best available proxy for what not to put in a no-flaky loop. Angular/Vue/Svelte additionally require the project's own npm install; Julia's dependency install can time out; Godot needs a running editor.
reference_evidence_note: Language servers without a readiness wait return PARTIAL RESULTS SILENTLY while indexing. An early-session 'no references found' is not admissible as evidence of no references — it is indistinguishable from 'not indexed yet'. A reference count taken before the index is warm is tagged derived, never probed, in the same evidence vocabulary the harness surfaces use.
rust_diagnostics_note: rust-analyzer emits diagnostics from several sources. Acting on source 'rustc' entries after in-session edits produces false positives. Rust is the product language, so this is load-bearing rather than trivia.

planner-v1.purpose: orientation before planning: read the symbol graph without reading whole files

planning-subagent-v1.purpose: same surface as its parent planner

implementer-v1.purpose: symbol-addressed edits and language-server renames, which keep the LS view coherent through the edit

builder-adversary-v1.purpose: fault injection at symbol granularity: replace a body, observe the witness

independent-adversary-v1.purpose: attack the decomposition, which requires editing to demonstrate a defect

independent-reviewer-v1.purpose: reads, references and diagnostics only; the rename and safe-delete wins are editing-side and irrelevant here

roles_note: read_only true must be set at PROJECT level in project.yml, never as a mode. Modes are switchable at runtime; project read_only triggers ToolSet.without_editing_tools(), which strips every ToolMarkerCanEdit tool — execute_shell_command included — and is applied last in the config fold so nothing re-adds them. Calling a stripped tool returns an error rather than being ignored.
enforcement_note: This covers Serena's tool surface ONLY. The host harness's native edit tools are untouched, so a role that may not write needs harness-level denial as well. C-SERENA-001 requires both.
unverified: Whether write_memory carries ToolMarkerCanEdit, and so whether project read_only strips it. Until confirmed, any read-only role also sets read_only_memory_patterns to ".*" — which is a regex, not a glob.
